title: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
summary: An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers. The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory. The attacker has since taken some of that data. cPGuard 5.88.25 and later versions remove the backdoor and the files the script left. Credentials the script copied may still work after the update, so any server that may have run the script also needs new passwords and keys.

title: CWP2Shell: The Login Page That Never Says No
summary: Today VulnCheck is disclosing ten vulnerabilities in Control Web Panel (CWP, formerly CentOS Web Panel), the hosting control panel that ships on a large number of internet-facing servers. They are being disclosed in accordance with VulnCheck's coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, and all ten carry allocated IDs through the VulnCheck CNA. The most severe of these is CVE-2026-73695, an unauthenticated remote code execution in the user panel of Control Web Panel. From that foothold the root-owned loopback user API gives two independent paths to root: its ungated routes (CVE-2026-77877) reach a command injection that runs as root, and a SQL injection in the API's authentication gate (CVE-2026-77879) forges past it to the same result. This was tested on the CWP7 webpanel 1.8 build on AlmaLinux 9, a build that already carries the patch for the last KEV-listed CWP RCE.

title: Russia-Aligned Gorbag Hackers Exploit WinRAR Flaw to Deploy Data-Stealing Malware
summary: A Russia-aligned threat actor known as Gorbag has been observed using simple information stealer malware in attacks targeting Ukrainian organizations. "Active since at least February 2025, the group has focused exclusively on Ukrainian targets, with a clear preference for law enforcement and justice entities, local administrations near the front line, and the defense sector," ESET researcher Damien Schaeffer said in a report shared with The Hacker News. The activity shares overlaps with a cluster tracked by the Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) under the moniker UAC-0226 and by Trend Micro as SHADOW-EARTH-066. Gorbag is known to be active since at least February 2025. A key tool in the threat actor's malware arsenal is GIFTEDCROOK, a C/C++ stealer that facilitates the theft of sensitive data from web browsers like Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Mozilla Firefox, such as cookies, browsing history, and authentication data.

summary: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code. "SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.

title: Barracuda warns of critical flaws allowing root access to devices
summary: Cybersecurity company Barracuda Networks warned customers to patch two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges. The first is a critical flaw (CVE-2026-116606) stemming from an Email Security Gateway (ESG) authentication weakness that attackers can exploit to modify an appliance's global configuration, while the second (CVE-2026-111560) lets threat actors with admin permissions inject OS commands that run as root. However, Barracuda said successful exploitation also requires access to the administrative interfaces of targeted devices and advised customers to use appropriate network access controls and restrict access to trusted internal networks to limit exposure.

title: What exploited vulnerabilities have in common: A data-driven analysis of real-world attacks
summary: The vulnerability landscape continues to expand. From 1999 through September 2026, approximately 383,000 software vulnerabilities had been disclosed across platforms and technologies, yet only about 2,000 CVEs (roughly 0.5%) have been linked to real-world exploitation. Those vulnerabilities follow clear patterns. Threat actors disproportionately target flaws that enable system takeover, particularly remote code execution, privilege escalation, and authentication bypass. AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploit development could further shorten the window defenders have to respond. Patching remains essential, but remediation can take weeks or months on critical systems, and some legacy or unsupported systems cannot be patched. Defenders therefore need to concentrate protection where it can have the greatest impact, considering both the likelihood of exploitation and the potential blast radius of a successful attack.

title: PHP2Shell: what we know about the threat two weeks later
summary: Late October brought several unsettling cybersecurity stories all at once. Among these were two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, which potentially affected about 70% of websites worldwide. CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 — dubbed PHP2Shell — could let attackers execute code on a server remotely, without authentication. On October 21, PHP’s developers released emergency patches for the supported PHP 8.2–8.5 branches and for the unsupported PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. Experts predicted that attacks on vulnerable servers would start within 15 minutes of the updates going public. Amazon even reported exploitation attempts four days before the patches came out. With all this in the news, some organizations sounded the alarm early. For example, in several countries, government service websites were taken offline as a precaution. Even Wikipedia’s project management and bug-tracking system suspended service. Nearly two weeks have passed since the updates came out, but according to Censys data, of the 46 million scannable servers running a vulnerable PHP version, 29 million still contain the flaws. Right after the patches were published, we broke down each flaw in detail and explained what companies and everyday users should do. In this post we cover what’s known about the threat today, and what extra steps businesses need to take.

title: Prompt Adware: How Hidden AI Instructions Could Create a New Enterprise Security Risk
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) discovered Haiou, an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that persistently modifies an AI agent’s trusted instructions to inject advertisements for a third-party AI gateway. CPR calls this behavior “prompt adware,” highlighting how natural-language prompts and configuration files can quietly influence an AI agent’s future behavior without traditional executable code. While the advertisement itself is relatively simple, the technique raises a broader concern for organizations adopting AI agents: how much visibility do they have into the third-party prompts, Skills and configurations influencing the AI systems they trust? Key Findings - CPR identified “prompt adware,” where trusted AI instructions are persistently modified through natural language to influence future outputs. - Haiou goes beyond jailbreaking Codex, modifying global agent instructions so common greetings trigger an advertisement for a third-party AI gateway. - The same persistence mechanism could enable less visible manipulation, including steering recommendations, promoting services or biasing technical advice without the user’s awareness. - The finding highlights a visibility challenge for AI adoption, as prompts, Skills and configurations become part of the broader ecosystem influencing agent behavior. - The potential business impact extends to confidential information, particularly if trusted third-party AI components are abused to perform malicious actions or exfiltrate sensitive data.

Check Point Research (CPR) discovered Haiou, an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that persistently modifies an AI agent’s trusted instructions to inject advertisements for a third-party AI gateway. CPR calls this behavior “prompt adware,” highlighting how natural-language prompts and configuration files can quietly influence an AI agent’s future behavior without traditional executable code.

- CPR identified “prompt adware,” where trusted AI instructions are persistently modified through natural language to influence future outputs.

- The same persistence mechanism could enable less visible manipulation, including steering recommendations, promoting services or biasing technical advice without the user’s awareness.

- The finding highlights a visibility challenge for AI adoption, as prompts, Skills and configurations become part of the broader ecosystem influencing agent behavior.

- The potential business impact extends to confidential information, particularly if trusted third-party AI components are abused to perform malicious actions or exfiltrate sensitive data.

title: Suomen tukema rahasto auttaa tunnistamaan Ukrainan sodan vainajia
summary: 3.11.2026 Uutiset Suomen tukema rahasto auttaa tunnistamaan Ukrainan sodan vainajia Ukrainassa toimiva uusi DNA-laboratorio on auttanut tunnistamaan lähes 200 sodassa kadonnutta henkilöä kolmen ensimmäisen toimintakuukautensa aikana. Laboratorion perustamista on tuettu Partnership Fund for a Resilient Ukraine (PFRU) -rahastosta, jota Suomi rahoittaa yhteensä 8,8 miljoonalla eurolla vuosina 2022–2027 osana Suomen kahdenvälistä kehitysyhteistyötä Ukrainassa. Suomen lisäksi rahastoa rahoittavat Viro, Ruotsi, Norja, Sveitsi, Iso-Britannia ja Kanada. Suomen Kiovan-suurlähetystön edustajat vierailivat lokakuussa 2026 PFRU-rahaston tukemassa DNA-laboratoriossa Ukrainassa yhdessä rahaston ja ukrainalaisten viranomaisten edustajien kanssa. Kuva: Suomen Kiovan-suurlähetystö. DNA-laboratorio nopeuttaa vainajien tunnistamista Ukrainassa on tällä hetkellä yli 100 000 sotaan liittyvää kadonnutta henkilöä, ja yli 18 000 vainajaa odottaa tunnistamista. Kadonneet henkilöt ovat valtaosin rintamalla kadonneita sotilaita. Rikosteknisten laboratorioiden määrä on yli kaksinkertaistunut hyökkäyssodan alkamisen jälkeen. PFRU on tukenut DNA-laboratorion perustamista yhden Ukrainassa toimivan alueellisen rikosteknisen laboratorion yhteyteen. Uusi alueellinen DNA-laboratorio on mahdollistanut vainajilta otettujen näytteiden tutkimisen paikallisesti ja auttanut purkamaan tunnistustutkimusten ruuhkaa kasvavan tarpeen keskellä. Laboratorion kolmen ensimmäisen toimintakuukauden aikana on pystytty tunnistamaan lähes 200 kadonnutta henkilöä. Laboratorion toiminta kuuluu Ukrainan sisäministeriön alaiseen asiantuntijapalveluun (Expert Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine), joka muodostaa maan laajimman valtiollisten oikeuslääketieteellisten ja rikosteknisten asiantuntijalaitosten verkoston. PFRU:n tavoitteena on tukea yhteiskunnallista vakautta erityisesti Ukrainan itä- ja eteläosissa sekä miehityksestä vapautetuilla alueilla, jotka ovat kärsineet merkittävimpiä vahinkoja Venäjän hyökkäyssodan seurauksena. Rahaston tuella vahvistetaan alueiden ja yhteisöjen kriisikestävyyttä tukemalla varhaista toipumista sekä vastaamalla akuutteihin peruspalvelu- ja hätäaputarpeisiin. Kadonneiden tunnistaminen on monivaiheista Kadonneen etsintä käynnistyy omaisten tekemästä ilmoituksesta, jolloin heiltä otetaan DNA-näyte vertailua varten. Omaiset toivovat mahdollisimman avointa tietoa tunnistusprosessista ja sen etenemisestä. Vainajien tunnistaminen on monivaiheinen prosessi, johon kuuluu myös vainajien evakuointi rintamalinjan läheisyydestä. Tunnistamista hankaloittavat pitkät evakuointiajat sekä näytteiden kontaminoituminen ja sekoittuminen evakuoinnin yhteydessä. DNA-testien lisäksi tunnistamisessa tehdään monenlaista asiantuntijayhteistyötä muun muassa tatuointien rekonstruoinnissa ja henkilökohtaisten tavaroiden, kuten sormusten, ennallistamisessa. Omaisten DNA-näytteitä verrataan vainajilta otettuihin näytteisiin sekä paikallisesti että valtakunnallisesti. Kaikille vainajilta otetuille DNA-näytteille ei kuitenkaan löydy vastaavuutta tietokannasta. Tämä voi johtua esimerkiksi siitä, että kadonneen omaiset asuvat miehitetyillä alueilla, jolloin vertailunäytteitä ei ole mahdollista saada, tai siitä, että kadonnut on toisen maan kansalainen. Kadonneiden kohtaloiden selvittäminen on tärkeää sekä vastuuvelvollisuuden toteutumisen että omaisten henkisen kestävyyden kannalta. Tieto läheisen kohtalosta voi päättää pitkän epävarmuuden ja auttaa omaisia aloittamaan surutyön.

title: Exploitation Targeting Node-RED, a Tool Embedded in ICS Products
summary: On October 30, 2026, one of our canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115, an unauthenticated Node-RED admin API flaw, to deploy a flow that downloads and runs a Linux bot. We did not retrieve or analyze the bot binary itself, so we make no claims about its capabilities.

title: Government Linux Servers Targeted With SysGoRAT and Suspected AI-Generated Scripts
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a cyber espionage campaign specifically targeting Linux infrastructure associated with government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure. The activity, observed by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 between October 2025 and April 2026, has been tracked under the moniker CL-UNK-1211, where "CL" refers to cluster and "UNK" stands for unknown motivation. A notable aspect of the campaign concerns the use of large language models (LLMs) and/or automated artificial intelligence (AI) agents to generate payloads and execute malicious code. "The attackers behind this cluster of activity focused on Linux environments to conduct extensive reconnaissance and maintain persistent network access to support intelligence-gathering," researchers Roey Porat and Tom Fakterman said. "The attackers attempted to dump sensitive databases and exfiltrate government mailboxes to access social media accounts." The campaign employs a "versatile operational playbook," leveraging a combination of open-source tools, custom cross-platform backdoors, and web shells to maintain access. Another hallmark involves attempts to disable endpoint protections, wipe system logs, and plant deceptive red-team markers so as to disguise the activity as a legitimate security assessment.

title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. "VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine," Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman said. To make this information more valuable, the malware uses stolen session access to search the victim's Gmail account for receipts to corroborate the home address by extracting emails related to Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal.

summary: Over 1,000 Internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity flaw actively exploited in remote code execution attacks. title: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
summary: Mandiant responded to multiple incidents in 2026 in which threat actors hijacked enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs), a tactic known as "LLMJacking." Spanning a variety of cloud and LLM providers, these intrusions impacted organizations in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours. Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked.

title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
summary: Last week, Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor which enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM). Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices. These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices. We also took action to disrupt the command and control (C2) domains that operate these affiliate modules. Because these affiliates each have diversified distribution channels for their modules beyond XCPE, we assess that taking down their C2 domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices. We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates. We believe this campaign wasn’t an isolated rogue insider or a development oversight. As a result, Google has cut ties with Videostrong and banned them from making devices with preloaded Google apps.

title: BITTER Expands Its Arsenal with PapRAT
summary: BITTER is a suspected South Asian cyberespionage group active since at least 2013, with a history of targeting the government, energy, and engineering sectors. Over the past several months, FortiGuard Labs has tracked a campaign targeting South Asian organizations that uses PowerShell scripts and a custom remote access trojan (RAT), which we call PapRAT, to establish persistent access to victim environments. Based on lure filenames, command-and-control (C2) communication patterns, file metadata, and malware analysis, we attribute this activity to BITTER with high confidence. The campaign uses three distinct infection chains. The first uses a malicious LNK file that abuses the native Windows ftp.exe utility to execute scripts and create scheduled tasks that maintain contact with the attacker’s C2 server. The second uses a VHDX disk image containing a LNK file that opens a decoy spreadsheet while silently launching an MSI installer to deploy PapRAT. The third begins with a URL shortcut that retrieves a LNK file through WebDAV, leading to an MSI installer that deploys PapRAT. In this chain, PapRAT also delivers WmRAT, a secondary implant previously documented by other researchers.

summary: Recent intrusions in which threat actors have been observed weaponizing agentic frameworks to execute highly-automated intrusions has put a spotlight on evolving adversarial use of LLMs. In our September 2026 report, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) noted that forward leaning adversaries were beginning to transition from basic prompting to agentic workflows and LLM-enabled automation. Since this publication, GTIG and Mandiant have observed multiple threat actors abusing the open-source, agentic pentesting frameworks ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN in incident response engagements to conduct a broad range of actions across multiple phases of the attack life cycle. This activity has been seen across the threat landscape, as noted in a recent Wiz report. The emergence of Artex and similar agentic offensive intrusion frameworks underscores a broader shift toward threat actor adoption of open source multi-agent offensive frameworks, as well as potentially custom agentic harnesses. This represents a paradigm shift towards intrusions occurring at machine speed, with the automated chaining of complex attack paths scaling intrusions exponentially. While the mechanics of the intrusions remain the same, such as using compromised credentials and targeting unpatched systems, the speed and scale at which frameworks can exploit these known weaknesses introduces a new defensive challenge. Security teams, developers, and system administrators will need to fundamentally rethink defense strategies to counter scalable, autonomous software. We also provide defensive strategies from Mandiant Consulting. The defensive strategies suggested—control-plane isolation, short-lived credentials, least privilege, segmentation, and behavioral detection—are long-standing security best practices.

title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what has been described as a "highly sophisticated infection chain" targeting government organizations in Asia. The activity, detailed by Kaspersky this week, targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia and involves the deployment of a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework codenamed NetamLoader. The attack has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. Nor is it clear if the intrusion compromised more than one system and allowed the hackers to steal any sensitive information. The Russian cybersecurity company said the artifact was detected in the first half of 2026, packaged inside a Windows cabinet archive (CAB) file placed in a directory that stores Windows operating system update packages.

title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
summary: Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20–21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise. The attacks targeted CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw, repeatedly crashing GitLab processes, with some attempts coming close to succeeding. Although Alpine Linux found no evidence that attackers executed code or tampered with its software packages and releases, it could not rule out a successful compromise due to missing logs and a lack of outbound connection records.

summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two security flaws impacting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following active exploitation in the wild. CVE-2026-118527 (CVSS score: 4.3) - A generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that could allow a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. CVE-2026-104935 was added to the KEV catalog on October 13, 2026.

title: Cloudflare Reports 18.2 Million Network-Layer DDoS Attacks in Q3, Up 38%
summary: Threat actors are launching about 8,226 network-layer distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks per hour, Cloudflare revealed Thursday. The web infrastructure and security company said it autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer (L3) DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests in the third quarter of 2026. That amounts to 197,400 attacks per day, or one attack every 0.44 seconds. In comparison, a total of 13.2 million and 10.0 million L3 DDoS attacks were recorded in Q2 and Q1 2026, respectively. The increase has been linked to DDoS-for-hire booter or stresser services that are responsible for hundreds of thousands of attacks.

title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
summary: A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a recently patched Android vulnerability, dubbed "SMS of Death" and tracked as CVE-2026-58882, that lets attackers remotely disrupt cellular service or crash phones by sending a specially crafted text message. The zero-click denial-of-service flaw can interrupt ongoing calls, including emergency calls, without requiring any interaction from the target. What's worse, Android processes the message before it reaches the SMS inbox, leaving victims with no visible indication of what caused their phones to crash. According to the vulnerability researcher, Mark Blah, Google reportedly patched the vulnerability in its October 2026 Android security updates for Android 14 through 17. However, the flaw is not listed in Google's October security bulletin, and older Android 12 and 13 devices remain vulnerable because they did not receive the fix.

title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
summary: Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, also affects ordinary TCP connections, although remote code execution has not been publicly demonstrated on servers without an MPTCP listener. Multipath TCP (MPTCP) is a TCP feature that lets a single connection use multiple network paths at the same time to improve performance and reliability. It is commonly used in environments where devices have multiple network connections, such as Wi-Fi and cellular networks.

title: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
summary: On October 29, 2026, Cursor reported that a tampered copy of Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code, versions 2.1.313 and 2.1.312) was available and served in the Cursor extension marketplace for a few hours to attempt a supply-chain attack on Cursor users. Cursor reports that it was live from about 2:27 AM to 1:35 PM Pacific Daylight Time (PDT). We have confirmed that the malicious packages found on Cursor marketplace were never published nor distributed from Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace and from npm @antropic-ai/claude-code, which were not affected by this incident. Anthropic confirmed to Microsoft that their systems were not compromised and they did not develop the malicious package posted in Cursor marketplace. At this time, all evidence suggests that the incident is limited to Cursor marketplace. Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed the injected JavaScript embedded in the malicious extension package. The injected loader runs when the extension module loads and attempts to add an attacker-controlled Secure Shell (SSH) key, enable the local SSH service, establish reverse SSH forwarding, configure persistence, and report host details. Successful remote access depends on host privileges, SSH configuration, and the attacker’s server configuration; however, the loader may still write keys and persistence artifacts even when tunnel access fails.

title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
summary: VOLTA is a mature stealer implant with an optional AI-integration layer. After stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets, VOLTA sends a structured evidence bundle to an LLM to rank the victim’s assets by monetization value. - If a model refuses to perform the target assessment, VOLTA fails over to a three-model chain, implying a direct engineering effort and expectation of hitting model guardrails. - This stealer is self-deleting, and there is no attacker-owned infrastructure. The novelty in the AI-integration is that it is not supporting a traditional malware capability but working as an intelligence analyst on behalf of the operator.
